content:
Update (11 p.m. ET): Apple's System Status page shows all issues are resolved. Below is the original report.

Just a week later, Apple is experiencing another major service outage, affecting both end users and developers. Details below.

According to Apple's System Status page, the following services are experiencing partial outages:

  • App Store: Some users are affected. Users may be unable to make purchases in the iTunes Store, Mac App Store, and App Store.
  • AppleCare on Device: All users are affected. AppleCare purchasing services are temporarily unavailable.
  • iTunes Store: Some users are affected. Users may be unable to make purchases in the iTunes Store, Mac App Store, and App Store.
  • Mac App Store: Some users are affected. Users may be unable to make purchases in the iTunes Store, Mac App Store, and App Store.
  • Subscription Purchases: Some users are affected. Users may experience intermittent issues with this service.

All issues began at 7:40 p.m. ET and remain unresolved as of now. Additionally, Apple's Developer System Status page lists two ongoing issues that began at 7:20 p.m. ET:

  • App Store – Advanced Commerce API: Some users are affected. Affected services: App Store – Advanced Commerce API, App Store – In-App Purchases. We are performing emergency maintenance to improve system performance, expected to take approximately two hours.
  • App Store – In-App Purchases: Some users are affected. Affected services: App Store – Advanced Commerce API, App Store – In-App Purchases. We are performing emergency maintenance to improve system performance, expected to take approximately two hours.

Although Apple has stated the emergency maintenance affecting developer services will take approximately two hours, it has not yet provided an estimated resolution time for the outage affecting users.

This report will be updated as more information becomes available.
